facts.big: What are you doing this weekend?
facts.label: Planos de fim de semana
facts.sub: Conte seu plano com I’m going to…, convide alguém e, se não puder, diga I’d love to, but… e sugira outro dia.

facts.label: A pergunta de sexta
facts.sub: Na sexta é comum ouvir “Any plans for the weekend?” ou “What are you up to?”. A resposta pode ser curta: “Not much” ou “I’m going to the beach”. Depois devolva: “How about you?”.

facts.label: Graus Fahrenheit
facts.sub: O tempo nos EUA costuma vir em Fahrenheit: cerca de 80°F é um dia quente (uns 27°C) e 32°F é frio de gelar. Veja a previsão no celular antes de combinar praia ou piquenique.

compare.tip: When you decline, give a short reason: “I’d love to, but I’m working.”

pages.title: Sara’s weekend plan · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Friday afternoon in **Chicago**. Sara is excited. She works in an office downtown, but she is free on Saturday and Sunday. The weekend starts tomorrow! Her friend Evan asks, “**What are you doing this weekend?**”

“**I’m going to the beach on Saturday**,” says Sara. In Chicago, the beach is by a big lake. The water is cold, but the sand is warm. “Who are you going with?” Evan asks. “**With my friends**,” she says. “**Do you want to come?**”

pages.title: Sara’s weekend plan · 2/3
paragraphs: Evan is sorry. “I’d love to, but I’m working,” he says. Sara thinks for a moment. “**How about Sunday?**” she asks. “Sunday is great!” says Evan. “**Let’s have a picnic**.”

Sara checks the weather on her phone. Saturday is sunny and warm. Sunday is cloudy, but there is no rain. A children’s book, The Little House, shows people who swim in summer. Today the sky is dry. She puts sunscreen and two towels in her bag.

pages.focus: o som ng: going, working, bring
pages.title: Laboratório de sons · o som
pages.what: No -ing o final é um som nasal só, sem g solto. Muitos brasileiros falam “goin-gui” e “workin-gui”, com um g no fim.
pages.how: Encoste o fundo da língua no céu da boca, como no n de “banco”, e deixe o ar sair pelo nariz. Não solte a língua com um g: pare no som nasal.
pages.tip: Tape o nariz e diga going: o som deve parar. Solte e diga de novo, deixando o ar passar.
